definition: Generative artificial intelligence dependency (GAID) is an emerging artificial intelligence disorder where users have a compulsive reliance on AI tools for tasks involving creativity, critical thinking, and emotional support.
details: The excessive offloading of individual agency to AI may stunt psychosocial development and critical thinking.
story: Picture a novelist who has read so much that, given a first line, they cannot help but write the next one. It makes new things by recombining everything it has ever seen. The result feels creative because it is memory, reshuffled at speed. It is prediction pushed forward — each next word, or pixel, guessed from everything that came before it. That next-word, next-stroke magic is Generative artificial intelligence dependency.
